course: IR 105: Ranking II - Probabilistic Models & BM25
context: The crown derivation course: Probability Ranking Principle -> Binary Independence Model -> RSJ weight -> BM25, DERIVED step by step using the learner's strong probability (odds, Bayes, independence assumptions). k1 = term-frequency saturation, b = length normalization; then query-likelihood language models and why smoothing is mandatory (Jelinek-Mercer vs Dirichlet), and Rocchio/pseudo-relevance feedback/RM3 as the classical ancestor of modern query expansion.

topics: The RSJ Term Weight and Its idf Connection
laterLessonsCover: 02 From BIM to BM25: Term Frequency Saturation: The Role of k1, Length Normalization: The Role of b, The Assembled BM25 Formula, Tuning k1 and b in Practice
03 Language Models for Retrieval: Query Likelihood: Documents as Language Models, Why Smoothing Is Mandatory: The Zero-Frequency Problem, Jelinek-Mercer vs Dirichlet Smoothing
04 Relevance Feedback: Rocchio Relevance Feedback in Vector Space, Pseudo-Relevance Feedback and RM3, Relevance Feedback as the Ancestor of Modern Query Expansion
